findings.reason: ao-update.sh:43 (and ao-doctor.sh:31) still resolve REPO_ROOT as the script dir's parent, which is now packages/cli/src/assets (or dist/assets). Run directly, ao-update.sh cds there, passes the git work-tree check, pulls and builds, then fails at `cd $REPO_ROOT/packages/ao`. Only runRepoScript exports AO_REPO_ROOT, and the script tests always set it, so they don't catch this.
findings.claim: Relocated scripts keep the old `dirname/..` fallback repo root, so running them directly without AO_REPO_ROOT targets the assets directory instead of the repo root.
findings.evidence: Both scripts still compute `REPO_ROOT="${AO_REPO_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"` (ao-update.sh:43, ao-doctor.sh:31). That was correct at `scripts/` but is now one directory below `assets/`. When ao-update.sh runs directly, it `cd`s into that directory, passes the `git rev-parse` check (it is still inside the work tree), runs `git pull --ff-only`, `pnpm install` and the filtered builds, and then exits at `cd "$REPO_ROOT/packages/ao"`. When ao-doctor.sh runs directly, it picks source-checkout layout and FAILs every node_modules, core-build and launcher check. Only the CLI path, which now always exports AO_REPO_ROOT from runRepoScript, is correct.

findings.reason: update.ts handleGitUpdate does call handleNpmUpdate(opts, "npm-global") when hasRepoScript is false, and that path compares against the registry and offers `npm install -g`, so the behaviour is real. But the new test asserts this fallback on purpose, and with no story.md in the packet I can't tell whether it was asked for.
findings.claim: A git checkout whose dist lacks the bundled update script silently falls back to the npm-global update flow instead of failing with a rebuild hint.
findings.evidence: handleGitUpdate does `if (!hasRepoScript("ao-update.sh")) { ... await handleNpmUpdate(opts, "npm-global"); return; }`. hasRepoScript only checks `<CLI_DIST_ROOT>/assets/scripts`, so a checkout whose dist was built without the `cp -r src/assets dist/` step reaches this branch. handleNpmUpdate then compares against the npm registry. If a source checkout on main is not behind the published version, it prints "Already on latest version" and returns without running git pull or a rebuild. Otherwise it prompts to run `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest` (hard-coded npm, even for pnpm users). It also prints "--skip-smoke and --smoke-only only apply to git source installs. Ignoring." to a user who is on a git source install. No spec line or test shows this fallback was asked for; the new test only mocks hasRepoScript to false.

members.claim: When a git source checkout lacks the bundled update script, `ao update` quietly switches to the npm-global flow instead of failing with a rebuild hint, so the checkout is never updated and the user may be offered a global npm install that shadows their source launcher.
